block.name: Frame Gate CC
block.doc:
Periodic frame gate for 5G-like frames.
This block uses a simple time model aligned with UHD:
- "Sample rate (Hz)" (samp_rate) - "Active period (s)" (period_s): duration of the active frame where the RF transmitter is allowed to be "on", e.g. 10 ms. - "Gap after period (s)" (gap_s): silent interval after the active frame, e.g. 5 ms for spectrum sensing. - Effective period: T_eff = period_s + gap_s - "Initial USRP time (s)" (t0_usrp): absolute time in seconds corresponding to global sample index 0.
For each integer frame index k = 0,1,2,...:
- Frame start: t_k = t0_usrp + k * T_eff - Active region: [t_k, t_k + period_s) - Gap region: [t_k + period_s, t_k + T_eff)
Given global sample index n, the block computes:
t = t0_usrp + n / samp_rate
If t lies inside the active region, the block passes the input sample to the output. If t lies inside the gap region, the block emits 0+0j (DTX). Input is always consumed, so samples that would fall in the gap are deliberately discarded, as in a real MAC that does not schedule those intervals.
If "Burst length (samples)" is set to a positive value, it is kept as a reference for the active part. If set to <= 0, the block derives it as:
burst_len = round(period_s * samp_rate)
Typical configuration for a 10 ms TX + 5 ms gap at 30.72 Msps:
- Sample rate (Hz) = 30.72e6 - Active period (s) = 0.01 - Gap after period (s) = 0.005 - Burst length (samples) = 307200 - Initial USRP time (s) = 0.0025
This block does NOT insert UHD tags. It only shapes the baseband by gating the IQ stream:
- Active region: passes the original signal. - Gap region: replaces it with zeros.
To align RF timing, combine it with a burst-time tagger block that inserts tx_time / tx_sob / tx_eob tags using the same (samp_rate, period_s, gap_s, t0_usrp).
